title: 产品需求与验收
scope: Clarify an incomplete request, distinguish desired outcomes from proposed features, and define bounded acceptance.
routingDescription: Clarify an incomplete request, distinguish desired outcomes from proposed features, and define bounded acceptance.
useWhen: User asks for a feature but the goal is unclear
Scope expands without an observable success condition

distinguishFrom.criterion: Use user research to choose evidence-gathering methods or evaluate interview support.

diagnosticChecklist.when: When a user proposes a feature
diagnosticChecklist.check: Identify whose problem is being solved, the observed problem and the desired change.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: Preserve known user intent and label unsupported market assumptions.

diagnosticChecklist.check: Separate supplied facts, decisions already made and choices still open.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: Define a smallest useful deliverable using only known project context.

diagnosticChecklist.check: Translate the desired outcome into observable acceptance criteria and relevant failure cases.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: State how the user can judge the delivered work without assuming a full project specification.

diagnosticChecklist.check: Compare impact, confidence, effort and dependencies using explicit evidence and unknowns.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: Avoid spurious precision from invented prioritization scores.

diagnosticChecklist.check: Identify the one missing answer most likely to change the proposed scope or success criterion.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: Give a provisional bounded recommendation when useful information is already sufficient.

evidenceRequirements: Known constraints and decisions already confirmed
Observable desired result and material unresolved choices
riskRules: External publication and commercial commitments require separately confirmed authority

preferredSources: Supplied user evidence and decisions already confirmed by the project
First-party documentation for named product constraints and integrations
refreshTriggers: Current product constraints only when a named integration is material
knowledgePolicy.onMissing: Bound the conclusion and state which current source or evidence is needed.

examples.input: An agent proposes a full CRM while the user only needs to organize incoming leads.
examples.expected: Clarify the desired workflow and define a bounded first deliverable.
examples.reject: Invent a company roadmap and mandate CRM integration.

adaptations: Converted task execution instructions into conditional consultation checks.
Removed persona, memory claims, model selection and tool grants.
Replaced unconditional numerical targets with context-specific evidence requirements.
